Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National “Invest in Ghana, produce here and grow” – Ato Forson Urges Investors Source : Kareen Tei 17 November 2026 11:29am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has called on local and international investors to commit resources to businesses in Ghana, stressing the need to translate investment opportunities into actual projects that will expand production and create jobs.
He has also challenged banks and development finance institutions to move beyond investment discussions and work directly with businesses and investors to secure funding for viable projects.
Dr Forson made the appeal at the maiden Invest Ghana Summit, organised by the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), where he urged participants to use the gathering to establish concrete business partnerships and financing arrangements.
He said the summit should produce tangible outcomes, with investors identifying projects they could pursue and making arrangements for further engagements before leaving Accra.
The Finance Minister encouraged Ghanaian businesses to present their expansion proposals, assuring them of the government's willingness to support credible ventures seeking financing.
"To the Ghanaian businesses, bring the expansion plan you have been waiting for to finance and government will work with you," he said.
He also urged foreign investors to partner local enterprises rather than approach the Ghanaian market independently.
According to him, Ghanaian businesses possess valuable knowledge of the local operating environment and can provide the necessary support for international investors seeking to establish and expand operations in the country.
"To the international investor, meet the Ghanaian companies that know this market and that can help you build an industry," he stated.
Dr Forson directed a particular appeal to banks and development finance institutions, urging them to engage businesses and international investors to determine the financial requirements of viable investment proposals.
He said financial institutions must play a more active role in turning business opportunities into funded projects instead of allowing investment plans to remain at the discussion stage.
"To our banks and development finance departments, use this summit to sit down with both and work through what it will take to finance viable projects," he urged.
The Finance Minister's call places access to funding and private-sector investment at the centre of efforts to stimulate economic activity, expand industrial capacity and strengthen domestic production.
He further challenged participants to make the summit a starting point for sustained business engagements rather than treating it as a one-off networking event.
"I would like you to leave Ghana here in Accra a project you can examine and a meeting in your diary," he said.
Dr Forson concluded by urged investors to establish businesses, produce goods and expand their operations within Ghana, emphasising the importance of building productive enterprises in the country.
The maiden Invest Ghana Summit brings together local businesses, international investors and financial institutions to explore investment opportunities and develop partnerships to support Ghana's economic growth.
